newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sets telecom interconnection charges.
newsitem.headline: France sets telecom interconnection charges.

text.p: French telecommunications regulator ART set on Wednesday a catalogue of so-called interconnection charges for the telecommunications sector.
The list establishes the prices France Telecom can charge its rivals Cegetel and Bouygues Telecom for the use of its infrastructure.

ART said the prices were 6.09 centimes for local calls and 12.78 centimes for a single transit service and 17.57 centimes for a double transit service. The tariffs come into service on January 1, 1998.
The figures were included in a detailed document which included various kinds of fixed costs for leased lines and other equipment.
France Telecom had originally proposed 16 centimes per minute for local calls, 0.18 centimes per minute for regional calls and 26 centimes for national calls.
Cegetel is owned by Generale des Eaux, BT and Mannesmann AG. Bouygues has teamed up with Italy's STET.
